items.title: LLM Context (llms.txt)
items.text:
Following the llms.txt standard, ticket provides machine-readable documentation endpoints at root:

  • /llms.txt: Structured index linking to all markdown documentation files and guides with summaries.
  • /llms-full.txt: Consolidated single-file reference combining all specifications and guides.

items.title: How AI Agents Use llms.txt
items.text:
When an AI coding assistant or agent operates in a repository or documentation site supporting llms.txt: 1. Fetch /llms.txt to discover the structure and markdown URLs of all guides and specs. 2. Fetch specific markdown files or /llms-full.txt to load documentation directly without web crawling or HTML scraping.

Start with the SPEC: Section 1 defines what core does and its non-goals, Section 4 lists commands and exit codes (including tk start --claim). /llms-full.txt is regenerated from the docs with make docs-build.

items.title: Agent Execution Loop
items.text:
When operating inside repositories tracked by ticket, autonomous AI coding agents follow a deterministic 5-step execution loop:

flowchart LR
    A["1. Query Actionable Work<br/>`tk ready`"] --> B["2. Claim Ticket<br/>`tk start <id> --claim`"]
    B --> C["3. Inspect & Decompose<br/>`tk show <id>`"]
    C --> D["4. Execute & Audit<br/>`tk add-note <id> '...'`"]
    D --> E["5. Close & Unblock<br/>`tk close <id>`"]

items.title: The 5-Step Loop
items.text:
1. Discover Actionable Tasks: Run tk ready to list unblocked tickets whose dependencies have all been satisfied.
  2. Claim the Task: Run tk start <id> --claim [--assignee <agent-name>]. It atomically sets in_progress and the assignee (default: git config user.name, else $USER). Agents sharing one identity must pass distinct --assignee values.
  3. Exit 0: claimed (re-claiming your own ticket also succeeds).
  4. Exit 3: lost claim; the ticket is in_progress for another assignee. Pick another ticket from tk ready.
  5. Exit 4: lock timeout; another tk process holds the ticket lock. Retry shortly.
  6. Inspect Requirements & Subtasks: Run tk show <id> to inspect design notes, acceptance criteria, and child tickets. Decompose complex tasks using tk create "<title>" --parent <id> and tk dep <child> <dependency>.
  7. Implement, Verify & Record Notes: Execute code changes, run tests (make test), and append review audit notes via tk add-note <id> "...".
  8. Close the Ticket: Run tk close <id> to mark complete and automatically unblock downstream dependent tickets.

Tickets imported with tk github sync contain text from GitHub users. Review them before an agent acts on them; see Agent Guidelines.

items.title: Command Reference
items.text: The tk CLI covers the ticket lifecycle, dependency tracking, and querying. Every command accepts a full or partial ticket ID (tk show 5c4 matches nw-5c46a1). Run tk help for the built-in summary and the list of installed plugins.

items.title: Repository
items.text:
Command Description Example tk init [dir] Create .tickets/ with a closed setup ticket and .tickets/.gitignore. Safe to re-run. tk init tk uninit [dir] Delete the .tickets/ directory and every ticket in it. No confirmation. tk uninit

tk create also initializes .tickets/ (with the setup ticket) in the current directory when none is found.

items.title: Create, Show, Update
items.text:
Command Description Example tk create [title] [options] Create a ticket and print its ID tk create "Fix login bug" -p 0 -t bug tk show <id> Print the ticket (uses $TICKET_PAGER or $PAGER on a terminal) tk show tic-c83r2a tk update <id> [options] Update fields in place tk update tic-c83r2a -p 1 --tags urgent tk edit <id> Open the ticket file in $EDITOR tk edit tic-c83r2a tk add-note <id> [text] Append a timestamped note; reads stdin when text is omitted echo "Done" \| tk add-note tic-1

create options

Option Meaning Default -d, --description Description text --design Design notes --acceptance Acceptance criteria -t, --type bug, feature, task, epic, chore task -p, --priority 0 (highest) to 4 2 -a, --assignee Assignee git config user.name --external-ref External reference, e.g. gh-123, JIRA-456 --parent Parent ticket ID --tags Comma-separated tags

update options: --title, -d/--description, -p/--priority, -t/--type, -a/--assignee, --tags, --design, --acceptance, --parent, --external-ref.

Values are stored verbatim, including /, &, \ and |. Frontmatter fields (assignee, tags, external ref, parent, and other single-line values) reject newlines with an error. See SPEC §2.4.

items.title: Status and Claiming
items.text:
Command Description Example tk start <id> Set status to in_progress tk start tic-c83r2a tk start <id> --claim [--assignee X] Set in_progress and the assignee in one locked step tk start tic-c83r2a --claim --assignee agent-2 tk close <id> Set status to closed tk close tic-c83r2a tk reopen <id> Set status to open tk reopen tic-c83r2a tk status <id> <status> Set open, in_progress, or closed tk status tic-c83r2a open

--claim defaults the assignee to git config user.name, else $USER. It fails with exit code 3 when the ticket is already in_progress for a different assignee; re-claiming your own ticket succeeds. Agents that share one identity must pass distinct --assignee values.

Status writes and claims run under a per-ticket lock in .tickets/.locks/. If another tk process holds the lock for longer than TK_LOCK_TIMEOUT seconds (default 10), the command exits 4. See SPEC §4.2.

items.title: Dependencies and Links
items.text: Command Description Example tk dep <id> <dep-id> id depends on dep-id; rejects self-dependencies and cycles (exit 1) tk dep tic-2 tic-1 tk undep <id> <dep-id> Remove a dependency tk undep tic-2 tic-1 tk dep tree [--full] <id> Print the dependency tree; --full disables deduplication tk dep tree tic-1 tk dep cycle Report dependency cycles among open tickets tk dep cycle tk link <id> <id> [id...] Link tickets symmetrically (no blocking) tk link tic-1 tic-2 tic-3 tk unlink <id> <target-id> Remove a link tk unlink tic-1 tic-2

items.title: Queues and Listing
items.text:
Command Description Example tk ready [-a X] [-T X] Open or in-progress tickets whose dependencies are all closed tk ready -T backend tk blocked [-a X] [-T X] Open or in-progress tickets with unresolved dependencies tk blocked tk closed [--limit=N] [-a X] [-T X] Recently closed tickets, by file mtime (default 20) tk closed --limit=5 tk ls, tk list [options] List tickets; hides closed, limit 10 tk ls -s open -p 1 tk find <search-term> Search text across tickets tk find "authentication" tk query [jq-filter] Print tickets as JSON lines; the filter needs jq tk query '.priority == "0"'

-a filters by assignee, -T by tag.

ls options: -s/--status (open, in_progress, closed, all), -a/--assignee, -t/--type, -p/--priority, -T/--tag, -n/--limit (default 10), --full (no limit), --all (all statuses, no limit).

items.title: Other
items.text:
Command Description tk agent-skill [--install] [--path] Print the agent skill, install it to ~/.agents/skills/tk/SKILL.md, or print its installed path tk version, --version, -v Print version and project information tk help, --help, -h Print built-in commands and installed plugins tk super <cmd> [args] Run a built-in command, bypassing any plugin with the same name

A plugin named tk-<cmd> or ticket-<cmd> takes precedence over a built-in <cmd>; see Plugin Architecture.

items.title: Exit Codes
items.text:
Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Error: usage, ticket not found, invalid or multi-line value, or a ticket file that cannot be written 3 Claim lost: tk start --claim found the ticket in_progress for another assignee 4 Lock timeout: another tk process held the ticket lock longer than TK_LOCK_TIMEOUT

A failed write prints Error: cannot write ticket file '<path>', prints no ticket ID, and fires no hooks.

items.title: Configuration
items.text: ticket (tk) has no database, server, or config file. Behaviour is set through environment variables, and state lives in .tickets/.

items.title: Environment Variables
items.text: Variable Description Default TICKETS_DIR Path to the .tickets directory. Overrides discovery. Discovered upwards from $PWD EDITOR, VISUAL Editor for tk edit (EDITOR wins over VISUAL). nano TICKET_PAGER, PAGER Pager for tk show when stdout is a terminal (TICKET_PAGER wins). None (no pager) TK_ID_HASH_LENGTH Length of the random part of new ticket IDs (4-32). 6 TK_LOCK_TIMEOUT Seconds to wait for a busy ticket lock before exiting 4. 10 TK_LOCK_STALE_SECONDS Age after which a lock is treated as stale and removed. 60 TK_NO_HOOKS Skip post-write hooks for the command. See SPEC §5.1. Unset (hooks run) TK_HOOKS_SYNC Run post-write hooks inline instead of in the background. Unset (background) AGENTS_SKILLS_DIR Target directory for tk agent-skill --install. $HOME/.agents/skills/tk TK_SCRIPT Path to the tk executable; exported to plugins and hooks. Set by tk

items.title: Directory Discovery
items.text:
1. If TICKETS_DIR is set, tk uses it. Read commands fail if that directory does not exist.
  2. Otherwise tk walks up from $PWD to / and uses the first .tickets/ directory it finds. Git is not consulted.
  3. If none is found, tk create, tk init and tk uninit work on ./.tickets; tk create and tk init create it. Other commands exit 1 with Error: no .tickets directory found.

tk init (also run by tk create when it initializes .tickets/) records the project in ~/.local/state/tk/projects.json, which the Web UI uses for its project list.

items.title: File Layout
items.text:
my-project/
├── .tickets/
│   ├── .gitignore            # .locks/ and .hooks/hooks.log (written by tk init)
│   ├── .locks/               # Per-ticket lock dirs, self-ignoring (runtime only)
│   ├── .hooks/
│   │   ├── post-write.d/     # Executable post-write hooks
│   │   └── hooks.log         # Hook output (runtime only)
│   ├── myp-a1b2c3.md
│   └── myp-d4e5f6.md
├── src/
└── README.md

Commit the ticket files; .tickets/.gitignore keeps locks and the hook log out of Git.

items.title: Ticket File
items.text:
IDs are <prefix>-<hash>: a prefix derived from the folder name (ASCII letters, digits and . only; tk if none remain) and a random lowercase alphanumeric hash, 6 characters by default. Older 4-character IDs remain valid.

---
id: myp-a1b2c3
status: open
deps: [myp-d4e5f6]
links: []
created: 2026-10-03T12:00:00Z
type: task
priority: 2
assignee: developer
external-ref: gh-42
parent: myp-0e1f2a
tags: [backend, api]
---
# Ticket Title

Description text explaining requirements and context.

## Design

Architectural decisions, trade-offs, and technical notes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Feature implemented
- [ ] Unit tests pass

## Notes

**2026-10-03T12:30:00Z**

Timestamped progress update or review note.

Values are written verbatim and YAML-quoted only when plain YAML would misread them. Frontmatter values must be a single line; a value containing a newline is rejected with exit code 1. See SPEC §2.

items.title: Defaults
items.text:
• Priority: 2 (range 0 = highest to 4 = lowest).
  • Type: task.
  • Assignee: git config user.name when -a is not given.
  • Listing: tk ls hides closed tickets and shows 10 items. Use --full (no limit), --all (all statuses, no limit), -s all, or tk closed.

items.title: Optional Tools
items.text:
The core needs only Bash 3.2+ and standard Unix tools. These are used when present:

Tool Used for jq tk query <filter>; without it, only unfiltered tk query works rg (ripgrep) Faster tk find; falls back to grep git Default assignee (user.name); sharing tickets

items.title: Dependency Intelligence
items.text: ticket (tk) treats task dependencies as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), so tk ready can compute the next actionable work deterministically.

items.title: How Dependencies Work
items.text:
When ticket B depends on ticket A (deps: [A] in B's frontmatter):

  1. B is blocked while A is open or in_progress.
  2. tk ready lists B only after A is closed; until then tk blocked lists it with its blockers.
  3. Closing A unblocks B with no further action.
Relation Field Blocks? Command Dependency deps Yes tk dep <id> <dep-id> Link links (symmetric) No tk link <id> <id> [id...] Parent/subtask parent No tk create --parent <id>, tk update <id> --parent <id>

items.title: Adding Dependencies
items.text:
# The API ticket must close before the UI ticket is ready
tk dep web-ui3k9a api-7f2c1d

Both IDs must exist; tk dep exits 1 if either is not found.

items.title: Cycle Detection
items.text:
tk dep rejects a self-dependency and any dependency that would close a loop, printing the cycle and exiting 1 without writing. The check covers closed tickets too.

tk dep api-7f2c1d web-ui3k9a
# Error: api-7f2c1d -> web-ui3k9a would create a cycle: api-7f2c1d -> web-ui3k9a -> api-7f2c1d

Cycles can still appear through hand edits or Git merges. Run tk dep cycle to report them among open tickets; tickets in a cycle never become ready until one edge is removed with tk undep.

tk dep cycle
# Cycle 1: web-ui3k9a -> api-7f2c1d -> web-ui3k9a

items.title: Viewing Dependency Trees
items.text:
tk dep tree web-ui3k9a          # repeated subtrees are shown once
tk dep tree --full web-ui3k9a   # disable deduplication

items.title: Ready Queue for Agents
items.text:
Many agents can share one queue. Each takes a ready ticket and claims it atomically:

tk ready -T backend                              # pick a candidate
tk start api-7f2c1d --claim --assignee agent-2   # exit 3 if someone else claimed it first

A claim that loses the race exits 3; pick another ticket from tk ready. See Command Reference.

items.title: Installation
items.text: ticket (tk) has a single-file Bash core with no runtime dependencies. Plugins are optional; install only what you need.

items.title: Quick Install
items.text:
Clone the repository and run the modular installer:

git clone https://github.com/msampathkumar/ticket.git
cd ticket

# Full Suite (CLI + Web UI + Agent Skill) — default
./install.sh --full

Binaries are installed to ~/.local/bin/ (override with BIN_DIR). Ensure that directory is on your $PATH.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
Core CLI: Bash 3.2+ and standard Unix tools (awk, sed, grep, find, mkdir, date) on macOS or Linux. Python and Node are not used.

Optional tool Used for jq tk query <filter> (unfiltered tk query works without it) rg (ripgrep) Faster tk find; grep is used otherwise git Sharing tickets; default assignee from git config user.name

items.title: Installation Flags
items.text:
Flags accumulate, so any combination works (e.g. ./install.sh --core --github):

Flag Installs Requires --core, -c Core tk CLI Bash 3.2+ --webui, -w Web UI plugin (tk webui) in a local .venv Python 3.9+ with uv or pip --skill, -s Agent skill to ~/.agents/skills/tk/SKILL.md None --github, -g GitHub import plugin (tk github) gh (authenticated), jq --scion-taskforce, -t SCION Task Force plugin (tk scion-taskforce) Python 3.9+, scion CLI --full, -f (Default) Core, Web UI and Agent Skill Python 3.9+ (for the Web UI) --all Everything above All of the above

items.title: Examples
items.text:
# Core CLI only (no Python required)
./install.sh --core

# Core CLI + GitHub import plugin
./install.sh --core --github

# Everything, including the GitHub and SCION Task Force plugins
./install.sh --all

items.title: Quick Start
items.text: Follow this quick start guide to initialize a repository, create tasks, track dependencies, and launch the Web UI.

items.title: Step 1: Initialize a Project
items.text:
Navigate to your repository and initialize .tickets/:

cd my-project
tk init

This creates .tickets/ with a closed setup ticket and a .tickets/.gitignore that keeps lock files and the hook log out of Git. Tickets are plain Markdown files with YAML frontmatter; commit them with your code. (tk create also initializes .tickets/ if it is missing.)

items.title: Step 2: Create Tasks
items.text:
Create tasks with priority and tags:

tk create "Implement user authentication" \
  -d "Add JWT-based auth to FastAPI backend" \
  -p 1 \
  --tags backend,security
# myp-a1b2c3

tk create "Add login page" --tags frontend
# myp-d4e5f6

tk prints the generated ID: a prefix from the folder name plus a 6-character random hash. Commands accept partial IDs (tk show a1b).

items.title: Step 3: Add a Dependency
items.text:
The login page needs the auth work first:

tk dep myp-d4e5f6 myp-a1b2c3

items.title: Step 4: Check Actionable Work (tk ready)
items.text:
tk ready lists tickets whose dependencies are all closed:

tk ready

Only myp-a1b2c3 is listed; tk blocked shows myp-d4e5f6 waiting on it.

items.title: Step 5: Claim & Work on the Task
items.text:
Mark the task as in progress:

tk start myp-a1b2c3

When several agents or people share the queue, claim instead. The claim sets the assignee and status in one locked step and exits 3 if someone else already holds the ticket:

tk start myp-a1b2c3 --claim

Add progress notes:

tk add-note myp-a1b2c3 "Completed token generation logic and unit tests."

items.title: Step 6: Close the Task & Unblock Dependents
items.text:
tk close myp-a1b2c3
tk ready    # myp-d4e5f6 is now ready

items.title: Step 7: Launch the Web UI (Optional Plugin)
items.text:
If you installed the Web UI (./install.sh --full or --webui), open the Kanban board and DAG Mind Map:

tk webui

Open http://localhost:8475 in your browser.

items.title: Plugin Architecture
items.text: ticket uses executable discovery in $PATH to dispatch custom plugin subcommands.

items.title: How Plugins Work
items.text:
When you execute: 

tk <command> [args...]
The tk dispatcher looks for an executable named tk-<command> or ticket-<command> in your system $PATH. If found, execution is delegated directly to that binary or script.

To bypass plugins and run a built-in command directly, use tk super <command>.

items.title: Environment Context Passed to Plugins
items.text: When tk launches a plugin, it exports two environment variables: - TICKETS_DIR: Absolute path to active .tickets directory. - TK_SCRIPT: Absolute path to root tk executable ("$TK_SCRIPT" super ...).

items.title: Example Plugin (tk-stats)
items.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tk-plugin: Quick summary of open and closed ticket statistics
# tk-plugin-version: 1.0.0
set -euo pipefail

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--version" || "${1:-}" == "-v" ]]; then
    echo "tk-stats 1.0.0"
    exit 0
fi

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--tk-describe" ]]; then
    echo "tk-plugin: Quick summary of open and closed ticket statistics"
    exit 0
fi

TICKETS_DIR="${TICKETS_DIR:-.tickets}"
open=$("$TK_SCRIPT" super ready | wc -l || echo 0)
echo "Ready Tasks: $open"

Make the script executable, save it to ~/.local/bin/tk-stats (or any directory in $PATH), and run tk stats.

items.title: GitHub Import
items.text:
The optional GitHub plugin (tk-github) imports GitHub issues and pull requests into your local .tickets/ markdown files. The import is one-way: tk github sync only reads from GitHub (gh issue list, gh pr list). Local edits, notes and status changes are never written back to GitHub.

Imported text is untrusted input

Issue and PR titles, bodies and labels are written verbatim into .tickets/*.md. Anyone who can open an issue or PR on the repository controls that text. Treat imported tickets as untrusted input: review them before handing them to coding agents or automation (for example the taskforce tag), and do not follow instructions embedded in them.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
Before using tk github, ensure the following tools are installed and configured:

  1. GitHub CLI (gh): Must be installed and authenticated with read access to your repository: 

    gh auth login
# or export GITHUB_TOKEN="ghp_..."

  2. jq: Command-line JSON processor used for parsing GitHub API payloads: 

    # macOS
brew install jq

# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt-get install jq

  3. Git Remote: The local repository must have a configured GitHub remote (origin pointing to github.com/owner/repo).

items.title: Installation
items.text:
Install the plugin via the root installer:

./install.sh --github

This installs tk-github into ~/.local/bin/.

items.title: Commands & Usage
items.text:
# Import both issues and PRs (default)
tk github sync

# Import only GitHub issues
tk github sync --issues

# Import only GitHub pull requests
tk github sync --prs

# Target a specific repository
tk github sync --repo owner/repo

# List all local tickets imported from GitHub
tk github list

# Remove all imported GitHub tickets safely
tk github unsync -y

items.title: Data Model & Tags
items.text:
• External Reference: Tickets imported from GitHub carry external-ref: gh-issue-<number> or external-ref: gh-pr-<number> (the legacy external_ref spelling is still matched on re-sync).
  • Tags: Imported tickets automatically include the github-sync tag along with any GitHub labels (e.g. bug, enhancement).

items.title: Configuration & State
items.text:
• Authentication Priority: Reads credentials from authenticated GitHub CLI sessions (gh auth login), or falls back to the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable.
  • Remote Resolution: Resolves automatically from git remote get-url origin. Overridable per-invocation via --repo <owner/repo>.
  • Query Limits: Defaults to 50 items per sync. Configurable with --limit <N>.
  • Data Safety: Running tk github unsync strictly targets tickets tagged with github-sync, leaving purely local tickets untouched.

items.title: SCION Task Force
items.text:
Hand a ticket to an AI coding agent: tag it taskforce, and saving it starts a SCION worker. You review the worker's report on the ticket, then close the ticket, which stops the worker. Ticket in, report out: the ticket is the only interface, and the project does not need to be a git repository.

The plugin (tk-scion-taskforce) runs only when a ticket is saved. No daemon runs. For the narrative walkthrough, see the SCION Task Force Workflow. For design and internals, see SCION-TASKFORCE-SPEC.md.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text: Requirement Check scion CLI on $PATH scion --version Podman or Docker, running podman ps Python 3.9+ (PyYAML optional) python3 --version Model credentials for the harness gemini-cli: GEMINI_API_KEY stored as a Scion Hub secret (scion hub secret list --scope=hub). Other harnesses: Vertex AI with gcloud auth application-default login

items.title: Install
items.text:
./install.sh --scion-taskforce

This links tk-scion-taskforce into ~/.local/bin/. Keep that directory on your $PATH.

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
tk scion-taskforce init                            # setup wizard; offers to run `test` at the end
tk scion-taskforce test                            # end-to-end check through a real ticket
tk create "Fix the login redirect" --tags taskforce # the save starts a worker
tk show <id>                                       # read the worker's report
tk add-note <id> "Also cover the logout path"      # forwarded to the worker
tk close <id>                                      # stops the worker

items.title: Setup wizard
items.text:
tk scion-taskforce init runs tk init when .tickets/ is missing and scion init when .scion/ is missing. In a terminal it then asks eight questions. Each is a numbered menu: Enter takes the default (*), Other takes typed input, and q quits without changes. You confirm a summary before anything is written.

# Question Options Validation 1 Harness From scion harness-config list. Default gemini-cli, else Scion's default_harness_config Must be installed 2 Model The harness's aliases (small, medium, large) or its default. opencode also lists google-vertex/ Gemini IDs No quotes or backslashes 3 Google Cloud project Detected from GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT or gcloud. Skipped for gemini-cli Project ID format 4 Vertex AI location europe-west3 (default), global, eu, europe-west4, us-central1, us-east5. Skipped for gemini-cli Google Cloud location; AWS-style names are rejected 5 Opt-in tag taskforce Letters, digits, -_. 6 Max concurrent workers per project 1 (recommended), 2, 3 1–10 7 Privacy confidential (recommended), standard Menu only 8 Role templates recommended (default set), none, or a comma list Role names

Auth follows the harness:

Harness extra_start_args Credentials gemini-cli --harness-auth api-key GEMINI_API_KEY Hub secret any other --harness-auth vertex-ai ADC; provider.gcp_project and provider.gcp_region are passed as GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT and GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION, overriding the shell

init writes or changes these files:

Path Purpose .scion-taskforce/scion-taskforce.yaml Project config with every key commented .scion/templates/tk-worker-gemini-cli-with-api-key-auth/ Worker template: scion-agent.yaml, agents.md, system-prompt.md .agents/skills/tk-scion-*/ Agent-team role skills, if chosen (see Role skills) .tickets/.hooks/post-write.d/scion-taskforce The save hook .tickets/.hooks/.gitignore, .tickets/.gitignore Ignore the hook log, the hook and the log symlink

init also links the folder to the Scion Hub once (scion hub link). Dispatch links only a project that has a task force config and became unlinked. Re-running init keeps your config values and template edits. --defaults skips the questions and installs no role skills; --force starts over.

items.title: Lifecycle
items.text:
Every successful ticket write (CLI or Web UI) runs tk scion-taskforce on-save <id> in the background. It acts only on tickets carrying the opt-in tag:

When a tagged ticket… The task force… is open, its deps are closed, and a slot is free Notes "request noted", starts a worker, verifies it runs, then sets in_progress is ready, but all slots are busy Notes "queued (N of M workers busy)"; starts it when a slot frees has open deps Notes "waiting on dependencies"; starts it when the blocker closes gets a human note while its worker is active Forwards the note to the worker, waking it if paused gets waiting-for-review from its worker Pauses the worker and starts the next queued ticket is closed Stops the worker and starts the next queued ticket loses the taskforce tag or gains no-taskforce Stops and deletes the worker and notes it (a worker branch, if any, is kept) is deleted (seen on the next save or sync) Stops and deletes the worker

tk scion-taskforce gc deletes the stopped workers of tickets closed more than watcher.gc_retention_days (5) days ago.

Status notes start with **Task Force:**. They are written straight to the file, so they never re-trigger the hook and are never forwarded.

Writes that bypass tk fire no hook: hand edits, git pull and worker edits. A worker's report therefore lands on the next save of any ticket in the project, or when you run tk scion-taskforce sync. sync also checks each running pod:

  • A dead pod gets a "worker lost" note.
  • A pod whose Scion activity is completed, waiting_for_input or limits_exceeded has finished its turn. Its report is merged; without one, the worker is paused with a note, which frees its slot. Add a note to answer or redirect it.

To pick up reports without saving anything, keep tk scion-taskforce watch running in a terminal. It repeats sync every 60 seconds until you press Ctrl-C. Nothing runs in the background after that.

items.title: Git is optional
items.text:
worker.git sets what workers may do with git:

Value Worker behaviour off (default) No git init, commit, checkout, stash or push. Changes stay in the working tree and the report lists every changed file. PR reviews read gh pr diff without checking out. Works in plain folders branch Commits on the ticket branch (scion start --branch <id>), never pushes. Git repos only

items.title: Privacy
items.text: worker.privacy defaults to confidential. Workers are then told not to upload or publish project content, push, or comment on external systems. skills install drops skills that publish content, and status warns when the Scion Hub endpoint is not local. Set standard to lift these limits, for example to let PR reviews post a gh pr comment.

items.title: Role skills
items.text:
Every worker runs on the project's one worker template (how the pod runs). Role knowledge ships as skills (how to do the job). tk scion-taskforce skills install [<role>...] turns roles from scion-frontiers/agent-team into skills under .agents/skills/:

Folder Content tk-scion-<role>/SKILL.md The tk contract (wins over upstream: work alone, report in the ticket, follow the git rule, no push), the upstream persona (system-prompt.md), the role guidance (agents.md) and paths to its related skills tk-scion-<skill>/ Each skill a role references, with name: set to the prefixed folder name and its own LICENSE UPSTREAM.md (in each folder) Source commit, licence and every installed or dropped skill; marks the folder as generated
  • Default set: developer, code-reviewer, investigator, doc-writer, test-engineer, security-auditor, researcher, architect. Name others explicitly (for example qa-tester). Coordinator roles are left out because tk is the coordinator.
  • Upstream is fetched once at a pinned commit (--ref <sha> overrides), so nothing is downloaded when a worker starts. Per-role model and resource settings are not carried over.
  • Re-running keeps existing skills. --force regenerates generated skills (those with UPSTREAM.md) only; hand-made skills and folders without the tk-scion- prefix are never touched. uninit removes generated skills.
  • Offline or air-gapped: mirror the repos as <dir>/<owner>/<repo>/, then run skills install --from <dir>.
  • Git: tk neither commits nor ignores the skills. Commit them to share (git add .agents/skills/tk-scion-*) or keep them local (echo '/.agents/skills/tk-scion-*/' >> .git/info/exclude). If Scion gives a worker its own worktree, that worktree holds only committed files, so commit the skills to use them there.
  • The skills are plain SKILL.md files, so people and local agents can use them outside Scion too.

How the brief uses them (the brief names file paths, so this works with any harness):

Ticket Brief Tagged role:<name> (several allowed) "Read and follow .agents/skills/tk-scion-<name>/SKILL.md before starting" (mandatory) No role tag The installed role skills (and hand-made tk-scion-* skills) with descriptions; use one only if it clearly fits. Less reliable than a tag Tagged with a role whose skill is missing No worker starts. The ticket gets a note with the install command; the queue moves on to other tickets

Custom briefs (worker.prompt_file) get the same section through the {skills} placeholder.

Migrating from role templates. templates install and templates list still work as deprecated aliases of skills (removal after 2027-04-01). Old generated .scion/templates/tk-<role>/ templates keep working for a role that has no skill yet. To switch: run tk scion-taskforce skills install, then delete the old tk-<role> folders (uninit also removes them).

items.title: tk inside workers
items.text:
Worker images do not ship tk. At each start the task force finds tk on this machine and mounts it read-only at /usr/local/bin/tk in the worker. It checks $TK_SCRIPT (the tk that is running) first, then tk and ticket on PATH, so nothing machine-specific is stored in the project. The mount travels as a Scion launch config (scion start --config), saved next to the brief as <id>.scion-config.json. It also sets TK_NO_HOOKS=1 inside the worker, because the shared checkout's save hook needs the plugin, which the container lacks.

If tk is not found, or provider.mount_tk is false, the worker edits .tickets/<id>.md directly. Turn the mount off when workers run on a remote Scion broker, where your local path does not exist.

The brief, the seeded template and the role skills tell workers to use tk as their only channel:

Worker step Command Read the ticket and new feedback (again on each resume) tk show <id>, tk dep tree <id> Share progress or ask a question tk add-note <id> "..." Report tk add-note <id> with a ## Task Force Worker Report heading Hand back for review tk update <id> --tags <current tags>,waiting-for-review

Workers never close, reopen or create tickets. init updates the old report section of an existing worker template in place; role skills update with skills install --force.

items.title: Automatic actions
items.text:
The task force fixes safe, reversible plumbing on its own and records each fix. status lists the latest five under Automatic actions; logs has them all.

Action When Undo Add /.scion/agents/ to .git/info/exclude (Scion requires it in git repos; local, never committed) init, and before each start Delete the line Run tk init / scion init init, when missing Remove .tickets/ or .scion/ Seed the worker template; update its old git and report sections init Edit or delete the template Link the folder to the Scion Hub init; at dispatch only for a configured, unlinked project (provider.auto_link_hub) scion hub unlink Start the Podman machine (podman machine start); tk never stops it Before a start, when the runtime is down (provider.auto_start_runtime) podman machine stop Stop or delete a worker Close, untag, file delete, gc Re-tag the ticket

What only you can fix (Hub down, a runtime that will not start, missing credentials) appears as one ticket note with the next step, and under Needs you in status. Saving the ticket or running sync retries.

items.title: Commands
items.text:
tk scion-taskforce [--config <path>] [--dry-run] <subcommand> [args...]

--config adds a config file on top of the others. --dry-run simulates every scion call.

Command Description tk scion-taskforce init [--global] [--force] [--defaults\|--interactive] Run tk init/scion init if needed, then the wizard: config, template, Hub link, save hook. --global writes only ~/.config/tk/scion-taskforce.yaml tk scion-taskforce uninit [--global] [--yes] Stop and delete this project's workers (branches kept), then remove .scion-taskforce/, the worker template, generated tk-scion-* skills and the save hook. Asks first unless --yes tk scion-taskforce hook install\|uninstall\|status Manage the save hook for this project tk scion-taskforce test [--timeout <s>] [--keep] Create a ticket tagged init,taskforce, wait (default 600 s) for its worker to report back, then close it unless --keep tk scion-taskforce skills install [<role>...] [--force] [--from <dir>] [--ref <sha>] Install agent-team roles (default set) as .agents/skills/tk-scion-* skills; see Role skills. templates install is a deprecated alias tk scion-taskforce skills list Installed tk-scion-* skills and their sources tk scion-taskforce on-save <id> [--event <e>] Handle one ticket save. The hook calls it tk scion-taskforce sync [dir] Merge worker reports, pause reviewed workers and workers that stopped without a report, flag dead workers, start queued tickets tk scion-taskforce watch [dir] [--interval <s>] Foreground loop: sync every <s> seconds (default 60, minimum 10) without retrying failed starts. Ctrl-C stops it tk scion-taskforce dispatch <id> Start a worker for one ready, opted-in ticket now, ignoring the worker limit tk scion-taskforce status Settings, save hook, provider health, workers, Needs you and the latest automatic actions tk scion-taskforce list \| ps All tracked workers across projects tk scion-taskforce feedback <id> "<msg>" Add a review note, wake the active worker and remove waiting-for-review tk scion-taskforce attach <id> Attach to the worker; a paused worker is resumed first tk scion-taskforce pause <id> Pause the worker tk scion-taskforce logs [<id>] Show taskforce.log or one worker's log, including rotated .gz files tk scion-taskforce brief <id> Show the brief the worker was started with tk scion-taskforce trace [<id>] Show trace spans, optionally for one ticket tk scion-taskforce gc [--force] Delete workers of tickets closed more than 5 days ago; purge rotated logs older than 30 days tk scion-taskforce version \| help Version and active config file, or usage

The removed daemon commands (start, stop, restart, server, project) exit with code 2 and print what to use instead.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
init writes the full key reference, with a comment on every key, to .scion-taskforce/scion-taskforce.yaml. Files are deep-merged, low to high:

  1. Built-in defaults
  2. ~/.config/tk/scion-taskforce.yaml (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tk/)
  3. <project>/.scion-taskforce/scion-taskforce.yaml
  4. The file in $TK_SCION_TASKFORCE_CONFIG
  5. --config <path>

Commonly edited keys:

Key Default Purpose tags.claim taskforce Opt-in tag watcher.max_concurrent_per_project 1 Running workers per project. Workers share the checkout, so keep 1 unless you accept that watcher.max_concurrent 10 Running workers across all projects watcher.gc_retention_days 5 Days after close before gc deletes a worker provider.harness_config gemini-cli Scion harness provider.model blank Model ID or Scion alias; aliases are resolved to an ID at start provider.gcp_project, provider.gcp_region blank Vertex AI project and location provider.auto_start_runtime, provider.auto_link_hub true Automatic Podman start and Hub link; see Automatic actions provider.mount_tk true Mount this machine's tk into each worker; see tk inside workers worker.git off off: no git state changes; branch: commit on the ticket branch worker.privacy confidential confidential or standard; see Privacy worker.prompt_file blank Custom brief template; {skills} inserts the skill section telemetry.rotation.retention_days 30 Days gc keeps rotated logs

items.title: Logs and state
items.text:
Path Content .tickets/.hooks/hooks.log One summary line per save (git-ignored) ~/.local/state/tk/scion-taskforce.json Worker state for all projects ~/.local/state/tk/scion-taskforce/logs/taskforce.log Task force decisions and errors (logs) …/logs/otel-traces.jsonl, …/logs/otel-metrics.jsonl Spans (trace) and metrics …/logs/workers/<project>/<id>.log, <id>.brief.md Per-worker log (logs <id>) and brief (brief <id>) .tickets/.scion-taskforce-logs Symlink to the log directory

Logs rotate daily (UTC) or at 100 MB. Set TK_SCION_TASKFORCE_LOG_DIR or TK_SCION_TASKFORCE_STATE_DIR to move them.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom Cause Fix Saving a tagged ticket does nothing Hook missing, ticket not ready, or TK_NO_HOOKS set Run tk scion-taskforce status, read .tickets/.hooks/hooks.log, then hook install or sync Note: "could not start a Scion worker … podman" Container runtime down and podman machine start failed or is disabled Start the runtime, then save the ticket again or run sync Note: "not linked to the Scion Hub" Folder has no task force config, or the link failed Run tk scion-taskforce init once Note: "'.scion/agents/' must be in .gitignore" The automatic .git/info/exclude fix failed (for example, a read-only .git) Add /.scion/agents/ to .git/info/exclude, then save the ticket again Note: "role skill tk-scion-x is not installed" The ticket is tagged role:x but .agents/skills/tk-scion-x/ is missing; no worker started tk scion-taskforce skills install x, then save the ticket again or run sync skills install cannot download No network or GitHub rate limit Set GITHUB_TOKEN, or use --from <mirror> skills install: "exists and was not generated by tk" A hand-made tk-scion-<role> folder has no UPSTREAM.md Rename that folder, or install a different role Worker reported, but the ticket shows nothing Reports land on the next save Run tk scion-taskforce sync, or keep watch running Note: "stopped without a report" The worker's turn ended (finished, asked a question, or hit a limit) without the review tag Add a note to answer or redirect it; attach <id> shows the session Note: "worker lost" The pod died without reporting Inspect with logs <id>. tk reopen <id> (tag kept) relaunches; remove the tag to abandon test times out Worker slow, stuck or queued tk scion-taskforce attach <id> or logs <id>; the ticket stays open Resumed worker fails with a model error such as --model medium Older versions passed the alias to scion resume Fixed: start now resolves aliases. To restart an old worker, remove taskforce, run tk reopen <id>, then add taskforce again gemini-cli worker shows a "Topic:" line after a note, then idles The model sent an empty reply after update_topic Re-run tk scion-taskforce init: it adds home/.gemini/tk-system-settings.json and its env var to the worker template Worker fails to authenticate Wrong credentials for the harness gemini-cli: add GEMINI_API_KEY as a Hub secret. Vertex AI: gcloud auth application-default login and set provider.gcp_project Ticket stays "queued" All slots busy Check status; close or review a worker, or run dispatch <id> Error: "worker state file … is not valid JSON" Corrupt state file Fix or delete the file (a backup is kept), then sync

items.title: Live test
items.text:
After changing the plugin, run the black-box live test with real Scion workers in a scratch project (initialised, with tk scion-taskforce skills install doc-writer):

cd /path/to/scratch-project && bash /path/to/ticket/plugins/scion-taskforce/scripts/live-test.sh

It covers create, a note to a paused worker, close, reopen with a new note, and a role:doc-writer review ticket, and prints each step's time and PASS or the failing step. Outputs go to test-runs/<timestamp>/.

items.title: Uninstall
items.text:
tk scion-taskforce uninit                         # per project: workers, config, template, hook
tk scion-taskforce uninit --global                # global config
./plugins/scion-taskforce/install.sh --uninstall  # remove the binaries

items.title: Interactive Web UI
items.text: The Web UI (tk-webui) is an official plugin providing a visual dashboard running on default port 8475 (ASCII for T = 84, K = 75).

items.title: Visual Showcase
items.text: 4-Lane Kanban Board Interactive Dependency Graph Create & Edit Ticket Table & Filter View

items.title: Key Features
items.text:
• 4-Lane Kanban Board: Drag-and-drop tasks between Ready, In Progress, Blocked, and Closed lanes.
  • Interactive Mind Map & DAG Graph: Visualize task dependencies, filter by status, toggle top-down or left-to-right layouts, and expand/collapse subtrees.
  • Multi-View Switcher: Switch between Kanban, Table View, Dependency Tree Graph, and Timeline/Gantt View.
  • In-Place Task Editing: Edit titles, descriptions, tags, priorities, assignees, design notes, and acceptance criteria directly in the browser.
  • PR-Style Review Comments: Chronological audit trail for review notes and comments (Cmd+Enter to submit).
  • Multi-Project Switcher: Switch between repositories containing .tickets/ on your system.
  • Auto-Refresh: CLI and agent edits appear within about 3 seconds, without a manual reload.
  • Works Offline: All scripts and styles are served locally; no CDN or network access is needed.
  • Full-Width Layout: Views use the whole window on large screens.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
Install the Web UI plugin via the modular installer:

# Install Web UI plugin only
./install.sh --webui

# Or install as part of the full default suite (CLI + Web UI + Skill)
./install.sh --full

This installs tk-webui to ~/.local/bin/. Ensure ~/.local/bin is in your $PATH.

items.title: Server & Daemon Commands
items.text:
These match tk webui help:

# Foreground server (Ctrl+C to stop)
tk webui [directory] [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--reload]

# Background daemon
tk webui server start [directory] [--host HOST] [--port PORT]
tk webui server status        # PID, URL, directory, start time, log path
tk webui server stop
tk webui server restart [directory] [--host HOST] [--port PORT]

# Shortcuts: tk webui start | status | stop | restart
tk webui version              # also --version, -v
tk webui help                 # also --help, -h

# Run from a checkout without installing
./run.sh [directory]
Option Default Meaning directory current directory Project opened first (see below) --host 127.0.0.1 Bind address (see Security Model) --port 8475 Listen port --reload off Reload on code change (development, foreground only)

items.title: Which project opens
items.text:
The browser picks the first available of:

  1. ?dir=<path> in the page URL.
  2. The directory the CLI was started for (tk webui <dir>, else the current directory), served by GET /api/config.
  3. The last project opened in this browser (only when the server was started without the CLI).

items.title: Daemon behaviour
items.text:
• Start refuses to launch if the port already accepts connections, then waits up to 10 seconds for the server to listen. If the process exits early or never listens, it reports the failure and the log path and exits non-zero.
  • Stop and status check that the PID in webui.json is still a tk_webui process on the recorded port. If not (process gone or PID reused by another program), the state file is treated as stale and removed; no signal is sent.

items.title: Security Model
items.text:
The Web UI is a local, single-user tool with no authentication. It reads and writes ticket files, browses directories, and runs tk as your user, so it only accepts requests from your own machine:

  • Localhost only: Binds to 127.0.0.1 by default.
  • Host allowlist: Requests whose Host header is not 127.0.0.1, localhost, or the --host value get 400. This blocks DNS-rebinding attacks.
  • No CORS: The UI is served from the same origin as the API, so no cross-origin access is granted. Other websites cannot read API responses.
  • Cross-origin writes rejected: POST, PUT and DELETE requests with an Origin header that does not match the host get 403.
  • Safe rendering: Markdown is rendered with Marked and sanitised with DOMPurify; all other ticket text is HTML-escaped. A malicious ticket file cannot run script in the browser.
  • Pinned, vendored assets: Tailwind, Lucide, SortableJS, Marked and DOMPurify are pinned copies in tk_webui/static/vendor/, with versions and sha256 hashes listed in static/vendor/README.md.

Binding to other interfaces

--host 0.0.0.0 (or ::) exposes the UI to your network and disables the host allowlist. Anyone who can reach the port can read and change tickets and browse directories. Only do this on a trusted network; cross-origin writes are still rejected.

items.title: Configuration & State
items.text:
The Web UI manages its runtime state locally without requiring an external database:

  • Default Port: 8475 (ASCII T=84, K=75).
  • Default Host: 127.0.0.1 (localhost).
  • Daemon State File: ~/.local/state/tk/webui.json (records daemon PID, bound port, URL, and active project path).
  • Daemon Logs: ~/.local/state/tk/webui.log (appended; not rotated).
  • Project Registry: ~/.local/state/tk/projects.json, shared with tk init ({"projects": [...]}, written atomically).
  • Theme Engine: Defaults to Indigo (#6366f1) with light/dark mode support; preferences persist in browser localStorage. In light mode, container and card borders use high-contrast slate-300 borders with dynamic brand-color hover transitions.

items.title: Lanes and Blocked State
items.text:
Lanes follow the same rules as tk ready and tk blocked:

  • Blocked: an open or in_progress ticket with at least one dependency whose status is not closed. A dependency ID that matches no ticket also blocks.
  • Ready / Open: an open ticket with no unresolved dependencies.
  • In Progress: an in_progress ticket that is not blocked.
  • Closed: closed tickets are never shown as blocked.

items.title: Solo CLI Workflow
items.text: The Solo CLI Workflow provides rapid, offline task tracking for individual developers and terminal power users directly in the shell.

items.title: Lifecycle Overview
items.text:
flowchart LR
    A["tk init<br/>Initialize repo"] --> B["tk create<br/>Capture idea"]
    B --> C["tk ready<br/>Query work"]
    C --> D["tk start<br/>Begin coding"]
    D --> E["tk add-note<br/>Document"]
    E --> F["tk close<br/>Mark complete"]

    style A fill:#6366f1,stroke:#4f46e5,color:#fff
    style B fill:#3b82f6,stroke:#2563eb,color:#fff
    style C fill:#10b981,stroke:#059669,color:#fff

items.title: 1. Initialize Once
items.text:
Inside your Git project root:

tk init

This creates .tickets/. All task metadata is versioned directly with your code.

items.title: 2. Rapid Task Creation
items.text:
Create tasks with priority, type, and tags directly from the shell:

tk create "Add SQLite caching layer" -p 1 -t feature --tags database,performance

items.title: 3. Check Ready Tasks
items.text:
Query actionable tasks whose dependencies are satisfied:

tk ready

items.title: 4. Work & Add Notes
items.text:
Mark the task in progress and record design decisions or progress notes. IDs accept partial matches, so tk start a1b2 works too:

tk start tic-a1b2c3
tk add-note tic-a1b2c3 "Evaluated in-memory cache vs WAL mode; choosing WAL mode."

items.title: 5. Close and Unblock
items.text:
When work is complete, close the task:

tk close tic-a1b2c3

Any dependent tasks are automatically unblocked and immediately appear in tk ready.

Working alongside agents

If coding agents share this repository, use tk start <id> --claim instead of tk start <id>. It fails with exit code 3 when someone else already has the ticket in progress. See the Agent Execution Loop.

items.title: SCION Task Force Workflow
items.text:
This workflow hands well-scoped tickets to AI coding agents while you keep the review and the merge. Set up the plugin first with the SCION Task Force guide; it also holds the command reference and troubleshooting.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Dev as Developer
    participant TK as tk (.tickets/)
    participant TF as on-save hook
    participant W as Scion worker

    Dev->>TK: tk create ... --tags taskforce
    TK->>TF: post-write hook (background)
    TF->>W: scion start (verified), ticket in_progress
    W->>TK: report note + waiting-for-review
    TF->>W: next save or sync: pause
    Dev->>TK: tk add-note (feedback)
    TK->>TF: post-write hook
    TF->>W: forward note, wake worker
    Dev->>TK: tk close
    TF->>W: stop worker, start next queued ticket

items.title: 1. Tag the ticket
items.text:
Write clear acceptance criteria, then add the opt-in tag. The save starts a worker in the project folder. Add role:<name> (for example role:code-reviewer) to make the worker follow an installed role skill.

tk create "Add input sanitization to auth endpoints" -p 1 \
  --tags backend,taskforce \
  --acceptance "make test passes; invalid input returns 400"

If the ticket has open dependencies, it waits for them. If all worker slots are busy, it queues. Either way, a **Task Force:** note on the ticket says why.

items.title: 2. Review the report
items.text:
The worker leaves its changes in the working tree, adds a report note listing the changed files and tags the ticket waiting-for-review. With worker.git: branch it commits on a branch named after the ticket instead. The next save in the project, or tk scion-taskforce sync, merges the report and pauses the worker. To have reports picked up without saving, keep tk scion-taskforce watch running in a spare terminal.

tk scion-taskforce sync
tk show <id>
git diff            # worker.git: off (in a git repo)
git diff main...<id> # worker.git: branch

items.title: 3. Send feedback
items.text:
Add a note. The hook forwards it to the worker, wakes it and removes waiting-for-review.

tk add-note <id> "Also reject empty usernames"

tk scion-taskforce feedback <id> "..." does the same in one command. For a live conversation, run tk scion-taskforce attach <id>.

items.title: 4. Close the ticket
items.text:
Commit or merge the changes the usual way, then close the ticket. Closing stops the worker, unblocks dependent tickets and starts the next queued one.

tk close <id>

tk scion-taskforce gc deletes the stopped worker 5 days later. A worker branch, if any, is kept.

items.text: The Web UI & Kanban Workflow combines the command-line speed of tk with an interactive browser-based dashboard running on port 8475.

items.title: 1. Launch the Background Daemon
items.text:
Run the web dashboard persistently in the background, for the current directory or a given project:

tk webui server start              # or: tk webui server start /path/to/repo

Start fails with the log path if port 8475 is already in use; pass --port to pick another.

Check status or logs at any time:

tk webui server status

items.title: 2. Visualize Sprint & Mind Map
items.text:
Open http://localhost:8475 in your browser:

  • Switch to Mind Map View to inspect dependencies, parent-child task links, and critical paths.
  • Switch to Kanban Board to drag tasks between Ready, In Progress, Blocked, and Closed lanes. Blocked and Ready match tk blocked and tk ready.
  • Leave the tab open while you or your agents work: changes made with tk appear within about 3 seconds. Refreshes wait while a ticket form is open or a card is being dragged.
  • Open another project with ?dir=/path/to/repo in the URL or the folder picker.

items.title: 3. Review & Audit Notes
items.text:
• Open any task drawer to review design notes and acceptance criteria.
  • Append chronological audit notes with Cmd+Enter (macOS) or Ctrl+Enter (Linux/Windows).

items.title: 4. Sharing with a Team
items.text: The Web UI is localhost-only and has no login. Each teammate runs it on their own machine against their own checkout; tickets are shared through Git. Binding to 0.0.0.0 exposes read/write access to anyone on the network. See the Security Model.
